rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (score 476.9, best so far): oval finished 20/20 with rms 0.012 m. The s-bend finished 4/20 (progress 0.71) and the slalom finished 0/20 (progress 0.18, about 0.95 line-loss events per trial). Iteration 2 to 3 was the only change that helped the bends, so the phase lead from forward sensor placement is working. Steering oscillation stayed moderate (0.18 to 0.33), so the controller is not jittering. The remaining failures are line loss on fast direction changes (slalom) and off-track drift on the s-bend, which points to too little look-ahead and too little damping for quick reversals. Changes: (1) move all seven sensors forward from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.08 m, the contract maximum, for the most look-ahead available; (2) raise kd from 0.9 to 1.0 to damp the faster phase response; (3) enlarge the sensor footprint from 0.012 m to 0.016 m, so that the tape stays under at least one sensor during sharp lateral excursions and the sum of readings falls below 0.05 less often, which should cut line-loss events. Kept unchanged: 7 sensors with x spanning +/-0.075 m, the weights, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5 and line_loss last_direction. Expected result: line_loss_events on the slalom below 0.5, slalom progress above 0.4, and s-bend finishes at 8 or more of 20. Hypotheses: (a) if line-loss events remain near 1 on the slalom, the larger footprint is not enough and the recovery mode or lower base_speed is the next lever; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.5, the 0.016 m footprint has blurred the signal and kd should return toward 0.9; (c) if the oval completion time stays near 1.85 s and bends still time out, base_speed can rise toward 1.7 for the finish-time term.
